authorities.name: Cooper v. Hobart
authorities.judge_or_panel: McLachlin CJ and Major J (joint reasons)
authorities.proposition: Re-articulates the Anns test into its modern Canadian two-stage form. At stage one, a prima facie duty of care requires both reasonable foreseeability of harm and proximity - a 'close and direct' relationship, tracing to Lord Atkin's description in Donoghue v Stevenson (not independently verified in this file), assessed via expectations, representations, reliance, and analogous categories (which are not closed). Only if foreseeability and proximity are established does stage two's residual policy analysis - whether there are reasons tort liability should nonetheless not be recognised - come into play.

authorities.name: Rankin (Rankin's Garage & Sales) v. J.J.
authorities.proposition: Applies and sharpens the Cooper/Anns foreseeability requirement: a business will owe a duty of care to someone injured following the theft of a vehicle from its premises only where, in addition to the theft itself, the unsafe operation of the stolen vehicle was reasonably foreseeable - foreseeability of one type of harm (theft) does not automatically import foreseeability of a distinct, more remote harm (injury from the stolen vehicle's dangerous operation). On the facts, a garage that left an unlocked car with keys in the ashtray owed no duty to a minor catastrophically injured when his friend stole and crashed it, because there was insufficient evidentiary basis connecting the risk of theft to a foreseeable risk of unsafe operation causing personal injury.
authorities.verification_note: The researching agent fetched the official bilingual SCR PDF directly from decisions.scc-csc.ca, quoting paragraphs 18, 23, and 26 verbatim. This session's own independent re-fetch of the same SCC URL returned HTTP 403; the core holding was instead independently corroborated via WebSearch against genuine secondary sources (law-firm case summaries), consistent with the researching agent's account of the 7-2 split and the 'theft plus foreseeable unsafe operation' test.

edges.verified_via: Rankin v. J.J. [2018] SCC 19, paras 18, 23, 26, per the researching agent's SCC-site fetch and independently corroborated in substance via WebSearch this session: expressly invokes Cooper's proximity/foreseeability framework, then sharpens it by requiring the specific type of harm alleged to itself be foreseeable, not merely the general risk category.

what_this_is_not: Two nodes covering the modern duty-of-care test and its rigorous application. Does not cover novel-duty policy considerations under stage two in detail, standard of care/breach, or any other Canadian Tort Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
